one_liner: Rust ANI and aligned-fraction calculator for genomes and MAGs; 20-50x faster than FastANI (C++), slower than Mash at querying.
what_it_does: skani computes average nucleotide identity (ANI) and aligned fraction between genomes, contigs or metagenome-assembled genomes above about 80% ANI. It has four CLI modes: dist (pairwise or many-to-many), triangle (all-vs-all matrix or sparse edge list), sketch (build a database) and search (query against a pre-sketched database such as GTDB). It replaces FastANI's role with a different interface and output; it also builds as a Rust crate with a minimal, explicitly unstable API, and has third-party Python bindings (pyskani).
how_it_is_fast: Instead of FastANI's Mashmap-style mapping of every 3 kb query fragment, skani samples sparse k-mer seeds (FracMinHash, k=15, c=125 by default), chains seed matches between the two genomes with banded chaining, and estimates ANI from the k-mer identity inside the chained regions, with no base-level alignment. A marker k-mer screen (k=21, c=1000, inverted index) skips pairs below about 80% ANI before chaining, and triangle computes each unordered pair once because skani's ANI is symmetric. v0.4.0 adds AVX2 seed hashing, an i32 AVX2 chaining kernel, a sorted struct-of-arrays seed index with galloping search, and LSD radix sort of anchors, all with runtime AVX2 detection.
when_to_use: All-vs-all ANI over hundreds to thousands of bacterial or archaeal genomes or MAGs (dereplication, species or strain clustering) where FastANI takes minutes to hours: 195 MAGs in 3.30 s against 2 min 59 s at 50 threads.
Searching a query genome against a large pre-sketched database (GTDB, 65,000+ genomes) in seconds with about 6 GB RAM.
Incomplete or fragmented MAGs, where pure sketch distances such as Mash underestimate ANI and you also want aligned fraction.
Memory-constrained runs (maximum RSS from /bin/time): 1.2 GiB for the 4,351-genome E. coli D3 search against 49 GiB for FastANI, and 10.2 GiB against 108 GiB for the RefSeq all-vs-all.
when_not_to_use: Pure speed screening where Mash-level approximation is enough: Mash dist took 0.26 s on D3 against 4.17 s for skani search, and Mash triangle 0.55 s against 3.30 s on the 195 MAGs.
Distant genomes below about 82% ANI: pairs under 15% aligned fraction are not reported by default.
When you need alignment-level ANI or exact parity with FastANI or ANIm outputs: skani is an approximation with a learned correction on top.
Pipelines pinned to skani 0.3.x sketches: the v0.4.0 sketch format is incompatible with older binaries, and older sketches are converted on every load with a speed penalty.
Eukaryotic or very repetitive genomes need the slower presets (--slow, c=30) per the changelog.

integration.form: CLI binary (cargo build, Bioconda at 0.3, prebuilt static x86-64 Linux binary) and crate (skani 0.4.0 on crates.io, API unstable)
integration.dependencies: Rust crates (bio, needletail, rayon, gbdt, bincode, memmap2 and others); a C compiler and make are required to build; tikv-jemallocator on musl targets
integration.min_toolchain: Rust edition 2021 (no rust-version declared); release profile uses lto = true and panic = abort
integration.platforms: x86-64 with AVX2 fast paths and runtime detection; ARM64 and other non-x86 builds work, with -i commands fixed only in v0.3.2 (May 2026)
integration.thread_safety: CLI parallelises with rayon via -t; library thread safety not documented

gotchas: Default ANI values pass through a learned GBDT debiasing model (195 trees, depth 3), so output is piecewise constant. Issue #57 found about 0.2 percentage-point gaps with no reachable value near 92.5% ANI. Use --no-learned-ani for the raw estimate.

Harness detail: the time_2328_results.sh in skani-test sets threads=1, but the checked-in times were run with -t 50, so the committed script does not reproduce them. FastANI --rl/--ql on 195 genomes runs both directions of every pair, while skani triangle computes each unordered pair once, so about 2x of the 54x is pair symmetry rather than speed per comparison.

The roughly 750x RefSeq figure (4,233 genomes) uses triangle -E on pre-built sketches, where the marker screen discards most unrelated pairs (bacteria, archaea, viruses, fungi). The same all-vs-all through skani search took 174.8 s, about 61x faster than FastANI's 3 h 2 min including sketching. The run's glob also passed markers.bin to triangle as an input file.

The v0.4.0 '~2x faster' headline is first-party PR #58 data on a 100-genome all-vs-all with unstated hardware: cumulative 1.48-1.61x single-threaded and 1.41-1.42x at 30 threads with default c=125; 1.91x only with c=30. The CHANGELOG mentions an exception to 'results unchanged' that its Minor section does not list.
pick_this_over_siblings_when: No sibling computes ANI; the closest catalogued tools (mosdepth for depth, rasusa for subsampling, sambamba for BAM processing) cover other pipeline steps. Pick skani whenever genome-to-genome ANI against FastANI is the job and approximate, alignment-free ANI is acceptable.
verified_claims_summary: The paper's skani-test repo ran a paper-era skani binary, FastANI 1.33 and Mash 2.3 (Bioconda builds) under /bin/time -v at 50 threads on an unstated CPU. Wall times: 195 MAGs all-vs-all, skani 3.30 s vs FastANI 178.96 s (54x, user CPU 46x); E. coli K-12 against 4,351 D3 genomes, skani 4.17 s search plus 3.55 s sketch vs FastANI 164.5 s (21x in total, of which 53.7 s is FastANI building its index); RefSeq 4,233-genome all-vs-all, 14.5 s vs 3 h 2 min. Mash sketches 2.7-5x slower (GTDB, D3, RefSeq) but answers queries faster than skani.
status_note: Actively maintained (v0.4.0 released 2026-10-11, MIT per the LICENSE file while Cargo.toml says MIT OR Apache-2.0), Nature Methods 2023 paper and Bioconda package. The benchmarks predate v0.4.0, and the Rust API is documented as unstable.
